sources.title: Himalayan Region, 1400 to 1600 A.D.
sources.note: Met chronology for the end of united Valley rule, emerging Kathmandu, Patan, and Bhaktapur kingdoms, Newari language, Buddhism, and regional art.

sources.title: Medieval Nepal, Part 1: Early Medieval Period 750 to 1530
sources.note: Detailed chronology from inscriptions and manuscripts, including the 1493/94 Bhaktapur grant and 1495/96 Gita Govinda colophon under Raya Malla.

sources.title: Yaksha Malla and the Division of Nepal
sources.note: Source-critical discussion of Yaksha Malla, Raya Malla, Ratna Malla, disputed succession, and exact manuscript dates.

sources.title: Divided Rule: The Malla Kingdoms
sources.note: Oxford academic chapter on the rival Kathmandu Valley Malla kingdoms, their political structures, urban cultures, temples, palaces, and monasteries.

sources.title: Nepal: The Discovery of the Malla
sources.note: Scholarly study of Malla history, Nepal as an India-Tibet intermediary, inscriptions, manuscripts, art, and discovery history.

sources.title: Two Medieval Nepalese Buildings
sources.note: Architectural study of Kathmandu Valley city-states, houses, public shelters, earth-and-wood construction, dating problems, and contested division narratives.

sources.title: Lumbini, the Birthplace of the Lord Buddha
sources.note: UNESCO evidence for Lumbini pilgrimage archaeology, monasteries through the fifth century, and stupas through the fifteenth century.

sources.title: Josef Peter Rindfleisch Collection of Nepalese Documents
sources.note: Heidelberg catalog context for Malla-period palm-leaf deeds recording land transactions, loans, property transfers, and legal agreements.

sources.title: The Newars of the Valley of Kathmandu: An Ethno-historical Summary
sources.note: University-hosted ethnohistorical synthesis of guthi associations, land, ritual, family membership, and explicit warnings that structures changed after the Malla era.

sources.title: Language, caste, religion and territory: Newar identity ancient and modern
sources.note: Cambridge study of Valley fertility, trade routes, Newari place-names, literacy, and urban division of labor.

sources.title: Beyond the Buddhist heartland: Magadha, Himalayan, and trans-Himalayan networks
sources.note: Peer-reviewed study of Kathmandu Valley city-states, manuscript colophons, donors, and religious and commercial circulation through the fifteenth century.

sources.title: Catalogue of palm-leaf and selected paper manuscripts in the Durbar Library
sources.note: Library of Congress digitization of a 1905 catalog listing Nepal manuscripts in religion, medicine, astronomy, drama, poetry, rhetoric, and politics.

sources.title: Indic Manuscript Cultures through the Ages
sources.note: Library of Congress record for academic studies of manuscript collections, scribal intervention, reading, editing, and medieval Nepalese production.

sources.title: A Study of Palaeography and Colophons in Dated Palm-leaf Manuscripts from Nepal
sources.note: University of Hamburg research on dated Nepalese manuscripts, scripts, scribal hands, colophons, craft, and the limits of palaeographic dating.

sources.title: Nepalese Painting
sources.note: Met essay on Newar artists, manuscript illumination, paubha painting, Hindu and Buddhist patrons, and fifteenth-century stylistic evidence.

sources.title: Bhairava
sources.note: Met museum record for Malla-period Newari copper work, used as a broad craft example rather than an exact 1490s object.

sources.title: Early Medieval Irrigation System in the Kathmandu Valley
sources.note: Austrian Academy project summary on rajkulo channels, hiti spouts, tanks, ponds, recharge, domestic supply, and excavation.

sources.title: Traditional stone water spouts of the Kathmandu Valley
sources.note: Peer-reviewed review of hiti chronology, water capture, conveyance, filtration, public use, and evidence limits.

sources.title: Reviving 1,500 Years of Water Heritage: The Hiti System
sources.note: UNESCO account of sixth-century origins, communal water supply, living heritage, and modern restoration, clearly separated from medieval household details.

sources.title: Traditional water systems of Kathmandu Valley
sources.note: Kathmandu Valley Water Supply Management Board publication on ponds, channels, stone spouts, recharge, and traditional water management.

sources.title: Ayurveda Cikitsa and Nidana manuscript record
sources.note: Institutional manuscript database record for an undated Sanskrit medical manuscript from Nepal in Nepalakshara script on birch bark.

sources.title: Interpreting the Ayurvedic Man
sources.note: Wellcome study of an eighteenth-century Kathmandu medical manuscript, useful only as a later comparison and warning against back-projection.
